_schema: canonical_findings v1 (assimilation-lifecycle-protocol 2026-07-15). Future experiments must state which findings constrain them. classification in the protocol's fixed set.

findings.claim: The flat-action SAC critic divergence (crit loss 0.66->72.7) was an IMPLEMENTATION confound, not fundamental: it came from the hardcoded initial entropy coefficient (alpha0=1.0) and learning rate (1e-3). With alpha0=0.1 + LR 3e-4 the critic stays bounded (0.18-4.61).
findings.scope: flat-action SAC on PlanarGrasp; the stable hyperparameters generalize to BC-anchored SAC refinement
findings.limitations: alpha0=0.1/LR3e-4 is task-tuned; NOT promoted to the global SACConfig default (would change classic-SAC behavior on other envs).
findings.framework_consequence: Coin-toss/flat SAC refinement drivers must set init_alpha=0.1, LR 3e-4 (recorded discipline). SACConfig now exposes init_alpha; entropy schedule via AlphaMode.

findings.claim: There is NO SAC integration bug in the actor mechanics: BC gradient is live and in the same action space as behaviour_clone (anchor MSE 5e-4 post-BC), sign correct, tanh log-prob sane, freeze-actor holds delivery (eval path consistent), overfit+reload exact.
findings.scope: SquashedGaussianActor + train_sac actor update
findings.limitations: mechanics-only; says nothing about closed-loop delivery
findings.framework_consequence: The integrity suite is a reusable diagnostic pattern (fixed-batch gradient/space/sign/freeze/overfit) for any actor-loss contradiction.

findings.claim: The 'BC penalty ~70 should dominate but the actor drifts' contradiction is explained by GRADIENT MAGNITUDE, not loss magnitude: |g_BC|=0.040 is 15% of the full actor gradient, dwarfed ~5x by entropy (|g_entropy|=0.205) and ~3x by -Q (0.116); cos(g_BC,g_entropy)=-0.20 (entropy OPPOSES the anchor).
findings.scope: flat-action SAC actor loss (entropy + -Q + demo anchor)
findings.limitations: measured on PlanarGrasp; the ranking (entropy>Q>anchor) is env/reward-scale dependent
findings.framework_consequence: Explains why TD3+BC (no entropy) holds while classic SAC drifts; motivates entropy-schedule component + rollout-anchor.

findings.claim: Entropy control (alpha fixed-low / annealed / ~0) does NOT rescue flat-action delivery: all ladder arms collapse the 0.417 BC floor online (S3 alpha~0 -> 0.000). Entropy explained the gradient magnitude but is not the delivery cause.
findings.scope: flat per-step action abstraction on the floorless PlanarGrasp env
findings.limitations: does NOT close the flat path entirely — the rollout-state anchor (F-SAC-5) is a separate untested lever
findings.framework_consequence: Flat per-step SAC pipeline QUARANTINED (registry); entropy schedule is a speed lever, not a delivery fix. Guard: do not deploy a flat per-step SAC actor as a coin-toss default.
findings.open_questions: Does rollout-state DAgger anchoring rescue it? (flat_sac_rollout_state_dagger_anchor, running)

findings.claim: The demo-state anchor holds action_mean AT BC on demo states (dist_from_bc ~0.002 across all 15 cells) yet closed-loop delivery collapses to ~0 ⇒ the destructive change is on ROLLOUT states the demo-state anchor never covers (covariate shift), not action drift on demo states.
findings.scope: any BC-anchored refinement of a reactive policy on a floorless env
findings.limitations: mechanism inferred from the dist/delivery double-signal; the fix (rollout anchor) is being tested
findings.framework_consequence: Motivates sac.rollout_state_dagger_anchor (EXPERIMENTAL). A demo-state-only anchor is INSUFFICIENT against covariate shift — future BC-anchor refinement should consider rollout-state supervision.
findings.open_questions: Confirmed positive pending flat_sac_rollout_state_dagger_anchor full run.

findings.claim: Delivery must be graded at the env's success_steps DWELL and the demonstrator ceiling measured FIRST: a hardcoded dwell>=20 (vs success_steps=5) read the 0.9-delivery demonstrator as 0.000, nearly mis-attributing a harness bug as a covariate collapse.
findings.scope: all coin-toss / flat delivery evaluation
findings.limitations: specific to dwell-graded delivery tasks
findings.framework_consequence: Canonical delivery metric (eval_delivery / flat_metrics) reads success_steps, never a literal. Measure the demonstrator ceiling before ranking a policy (CLAUDE.md eval-integrity rule, now with a concrete on-record catch).

findings.claim: The deployed FANUC pick-place policy is a Markov-mode hybrid-DAgger clone of the v3 clean expert on the require_settle task: 0.875 stable-place / 4.69 cm. The v3 expert resolves the clean-vs-yield conflict by a BASIN CONSTRAINT (route v2's clean transit into v1's unflipped grasp basin), reaching 0.906 / 2.16 cm.
findings.scope: fanuc pick-place v3+settle, fixed target
findings.limitations: raw state_dict (no metadata); target-blind; precision imitation-bounded.
findings.framework_consequence: controller.pick_place_hybrid_dagger_base registered DEPLOYABLE; loaded via load_pick_policy.
code_changes: already integrated (this assimilation added the compat-validated loader route)

findings.claim: Offline actor-critic (TD3+BC) COLLAPSES on FANUC pick-place: crit/act blow up, rl_refined (0.0-0.4375) <= bc_step0. BC/DAgger is the working imitation path; from-scratch/warm-start PPO also collapses to ~0.
findings.scope: fanuc pick-place env/reward
findings.limitations: scoped to this env; not a universal TD3+BC impossibility.
findings.framework_consequence: pick_place_td3bc + pick_place_ppo + pick_place_rl_sidebyside labeled NEGATIVE_DIAGNOSTIC/SUPERSEDED in the registry (kept runnable for repro, must not become default).

findings.claim: Structured residual RL HOLDS the frozen base 0.875 exactly (anchor + settle reward + PPO + mode-gate) but CANNOT improve it: a bounded action-residual cannot move a feedback controller's setpoint. Precision floor stays ~4.6 cm; SAC entropy drifts it.
findings.confidence: measured (delta x reward x mode-set grid, 3 seeds)
findings.scope: residual RL as a PRECISION lever over the frozen base; from-scratch RL NOT closed
findings.limitations: closure scoped to bounded residual over a frozen setpoint.
findings.framework_consequence: ResidualPickEnv registered RESEARCH_ONLY (not deployed); the closure is recorded so a later branch does not re-adopt residual-as-precision-lever silently.
findings.open_questions: From-scratch asymmetric actor-critic (not setpoint-bound) for precision — untested.

findings.claim: Pick-place precision is IMITATION-BOUNDED (~4.7 cm): no clone reaches the expert's 2.16 cm across feedforward, centered-target, and every recurrent cell (GRU/LSTM/peephole/LN/CIFG) — the centering is execution-hard, drowned in the BC loss. LSTM WINS reliability (0.917). Cloning a MORE-precise (centered Markov) target BACKFIRES (0.667/5.31, more-precise=harder-to-clone).
findings.scope: precision by IMITATION; a stateful RL-from-scratch or an obs exposing the PI integral are NOT closed
findings.limitations: the 2.16cm is a stateful-PI mechanism not observable to a feedforward clone.
findings.framework_consequence: Guard: a more-precise scripted target is not automatically a better clone target — do not re-run centered-target cloning expecting a precision gain. LSTM is the reliability-canonical recurrent cell.
code_changes: control/pick_place_laws.py centered laws REVERTED to tool-at-target (this backfire recorded)
findings.open_questions: DAgger'd target-aware/LSTM past the 7.5cm tolerance — untested.

findings.claim: Clones are TARGET-BLIND (the target is not in the base observation; the hypergraph is arm-only) so they MEMORISE the fixed training target — a moved target misses by 17.5 cm. Adding target feedback (observe_target: object->target displacement in node_features) + varied-target training makes a clone place at an ARBITRARY target (moved-target 1.45 cm).
findings.scope: fanuc pick-place arbitrary-target placement
findings.limitations: target-aware reliability borderline (0.71-0.79) at the 7.5cm tolerance.
findings.framework_consequence: env.observe_target_feedback registered CANONICAL (default off, byte-identical); load_pick_policy validates observe_target so a target-aware clone cannot be loaded into a target-blind env (or vice versa).
code_changes: gui build_scene builds env obs to match ckpt

findings.claim: Pick-place checkpoint provenance was UNSAFE: every FF/HSiKAN/TD3 checkpoint is a raw state_dict with NO metadata; the June checkpoints use an obs-72 schema incompatible with the current obs-90; and 4 uncentralized loaders (only the GUI's validated). A wrong-schema checkpoint could mis-load or fall back silently.
findings.confidence: measured (discovery over ~200 checkpoints; obs-72 vs obs-90 confirmed by tensor shapes)
findings.scope: all pick-place checkpoint loading
findings.limitations: provenance sidecar for the metadata-blind FF base still recommended (deferred).
findings.framework_consequence: loader.load_pick_policy (+ load_pick_actor + PickPolicyIncompatible) is now THE loader used by build_scene / render_trained / residual_rl._load_base; it FAILS LOUD on obs/action/observe_target mismatch (never a silent mis-load). Also: reports/models/campaign/* are galambos, NOT pick-place -> excluded from the manifest.
code_changes: gui/pick_place_scene.py, viz/render_pick_place.py, pick_place_residual_rl.py routed through it
findings.open_questions: Re-defaulting PickPlaceEnv bare constructor (still builds the anthropomorphic/v1/no-settle config) — deferred to a fail-loud guard, separate authorization.

findings.claim: The legacy success predicate (delivered = held-above-target) inflated 'place' rates until require_settle (genuine set-down: object at rest, released, within radius) was introduced. All pre-settle place rates are on the LEGACY metric and must not be compared across the boundary. The two '0.875's (v1-dirty-legacy vs v3-clean-settle) are different cohorts.
findings.scope: all pick-place evaluation
findings.limitations: require_settle default off (byte-identical legacy); canonical spec sets it on.
findings.framework_consequence: Canonical env spec is expert_version=3 + require_settle=True; PlacementPrecisionMetric/LiftPlaceMetric carry the divergence guard (a blow-up must not count as a lift/settle). Do not merge pre/post-settle place rates.
code_changes: already integrated (require_settle in the canonical spec)

findings.claim: A structure-aware elimination ordering cuts direct-solve fill-in on structured constraint graphs: min-degree gives 4.3x less fill than natural order on a cloth grid and 14.5x less on a pile, while every ordering blows up on a truly dense pile. Fill-in is the exact proxy for direct sparse-solve (Cholesky/LDL) cost.
findings.confidence: measured (fill/width/flops under 4 orderings x 3 system classes x 7 sizes, deterministic seeds)
findings.scope: constraint graphs of physics scenes (bodies=nodes, joints '+'/contacts '-' = signed edges)
findings.limitations: fill is a proxy for the factor cost, not wall-clock (that is F-PHYS-2); Sigma-deg^2 flops is the classic dense-Cholesky proxy.
findings.framework_consequence: The ordering + elimination-cost primitives are canonical (physics.structural_cost_predictors); solve cost is predictable from the graph BEFORE solving.

findings.claim: The direct-vs-iterative wall-clock crossover IS a treewidth threshold: structured/articulated systems (tw <= sqrt(N): chain, cloth<=N576, the real arm) solve fastest EXACTLY by sparse-direct (residual ~1e-16), dense piles solve fastest ITERATIVELY by CG (e.g. pile N=1024: CG 1.50 ms vs direct 7.82 ms, 5.2x). The fill proxy becomes seconds and accuracy.
findings.confidence: measured (SuperLU MMD_AT_PLUS_A direct + CG, median of 5 reps, seeded)
findings.scope: SPD/bilateral constraint solve (A = L + lambda*I over the constraint graph)
findings.limitations: A = L + lambda*I is the constraint-graph sparsity proxy, not the exact Delassus/KKT operator; CG is the bilateral-block analog of PGS; wall-clock constants are Python/scipy-prototype (F-PHYS-6).
findings.framework_consequence: Motivates the certificate-routed solver (F-PHYS-3): the crossover is predictable from the width, so it can be automated.
findings.open_questions: Grounding on the exact MuJoCo efc_* / KKT operator (box-pile) remains.

findings.claim: A single cheap structural number — the SBSH width certificate (a treewidth upper bound the scene already carries) — routes the constraint solve to the best of {exact-direct, iterative-CG} across the whole structure spectrum, with measured worst-case regret 1.13 vs an oracle that always picks the faster method (~1.0 almost everywhere). It recovers exactness where cheap (residual ~1e-16, where always-CG settles for ~1e-8) AND dodges the direct-factor blow-up where not.
findings.confidence: measured (regret over chain/cloth/pile x 7 sizes + the real MuJoCo arm; residuals exact)
findings.scope: any bilateral/SPD constraint solve exposing a (positions, signed-edges) graph
findings.limitations: W*=40 is one calibrated threshold (production: a fill-vs-iters cost model); the certificate's own cost is assumed amortised via incremental width maintenance (L5, conditional on edit locality; L6: adversarial global edits force Omega(sqrt N)); constants are Python-prototype (F-PHYS-6).
findings.framework_consequence: EXTRACTED to the canonical framework: AdaptiveWidthSolver + certificate_width in hymeko_rl/sbsh_scene/solver.py, exposed from the package __init__, imported by the physics_adaptive driver (no longer defined there). Future SBSH physics work imports it (anti-bloat).
findings.open_questions: A production cost model (fill vs iters*N) instead of a width cutoff; incremental certificate maintenance under adversarial edits.

findings.claim: The REAL frictional-contact solve obeys the same law: an LCP with Coulomb friction solved by Projected Gauss-Seidel over the Delassus-structured coupling has PGS iterations and #colours (parallel phases) CONSTANT in N on structured contact graphs (chain 19->19, cloth 40->43, arm 20; colours 3/6/3 constant) and GROWING on dense piles (iters 28->207, colours 4->32, accuracy 1e-5->9e-4, wall-clock to 2.2 s). So the width certificate predicts the real contact solver's cost and parallelism, not just the linear proxy.
findings.confidence: measured (PGS to 1e-6, median of 3 reps, seeded; the real MuJoCo arm graph included)
findings.scope: frictional rigid-body contact LCP over the contact line graph
findings.limitations: coupling is Delassus-STRUCTURED (line-graph Laplacian + I), not the exact J M^-1 J^T from an engine (topology faithful incl. the arm; entries a well-conditioned model); friction is a Coulomb box on one tangential; PGS accuracy is the honest ~1e-5, degrading with density; Python inner loop sets the wall-clock constants (F-PHYS-6, iteration/colour counts are implementation-free).
findings.framework_consequence: EXTRACTED to the canonical framework: ContactLcpSolver + contact_coupling/greedy_colors/pgs in solver.py, imported by the physics_lcp driver (no longer defined there). physics.contact_lcp_solver is CANONICAL.
findings.open_questions: Extract MuJoCo's true efc_* on a box-pile scene (the exact-Delassus grounding step).

findings.claim: The octree/spatial nested-dissection ordering is a WEAKER heuristic than min-degree on degenerate graphs: on a 1-D chain (true treewidth 1) it over-separates to induced width 2, while min-degree recovers the exact optimum (width 1, fill 0). It is a valid ordering (a permutation, and it does reduce grid fill vs natural), but it is NOT the clean structure-aware order.
findings.source_experiment: sbsh-physics-probe (2026-07-11, honest test failure kept as a finding)
findings.confidence: measured (elimination width under all three orderings on chain/cloth)
findings.scope: elimination orderings for the width certificate
findings.limitations: a production nested-dissection (METIS) would not over-separate; this is the octree-separator heuristic specifically.
findings.framework_consequence: GUARD: certificate_width uses MIN-DEGREE, not octree-ND. A regression test pins certificate_width(chain)==1 so a refactor cannot silently swap in the weaker heuristic. order_nested_dissection is retained as a measured heuristic, flagged in physics.structural_cost_predictors.known_limitations.

findings.claim: The SBSH physics numbers are a Python/scipy PROTOTYPE. The STRUCTURAL conclusions — scaling exponents, PGS iteration counts, #colours, the regret 1.13 — are implementation-free and citable. The wall-clock CONSTANTS are not: a Rust/C inner loop would cut them ~1-2 orders (exponents unchanged). No real-time (games/physics) claim may rest on the prototype constants.
findings.confidence: measured caveat (host: Apple M5 Pro, Python 3.11.15, scipy 1.17.1) + standard prototype-vs-native reasoning
findings.scope: every wall-clock number produced by the sbsh_scene physics modules
findings.limitations: n/a — this IS the limitation record.
findings.framework_consequence: Any future experiment that cites sbsh physics timings must state 'Python-prototype constants' and re-measure against a Rust/C core before a real-time claim. Registered in both physics solver components' known_limitations.
findings.open_questions: A Rust-core graduation (SpatialRegime + Yannakakis + the solvers behind hymeko_pgraph) would fix the constants — may touch CORE.YAML, escalate.

findings.claim: HTL existed as THREE non-interoperating evaluators: Rust hymeko_monitor (STL+Until, combinator-only, no text parser), Python hymeko_neuro/eval/htl (G/F only, scalar-smuggled structure, has a parser), and per-scenario `condition "..."` strings in .hymeko parsed by ad-hoc policy evaluators. They are unifiable because the coupling to RL is at the edges (signal sources + reward consumer), not the core.
findings.scope: the HTL/temporal-monitoring subsystem
findings.limitations: unification delivered on the Rust engine; Python consumers reconciled opt-in in v2, not retired.
findings.framework_consequence: One engine (htl.engine): a single parser + robustness algebra. New consumers import it; do not add a 4th evaluator.
code_changes: hymeko_monitor: formula/parse.rs, signal.rs, builders.rs; hymeko_monitor_ir crate; data/meta/meta_monitor.hymeko

findings.claim: The Rust engine reproduces the incumbent Python evaluator's robustness to 1e-9 on the real galambos spec (single-event robustness_at) AND on streaming HtlMonitor traces. This parity gate is the REQUIRED evidence before backing/retiring the Python RL path.
findings.scope: scalar-signal HTL (the whole production consumer surface)
findings.limitations: parity proven on the tested corpus, not every possible formula/signal; custom Python registry predicates are not backed.
findings.framework_consequence: Any move to make Rust the Python HTL backend (or retire pure-Python) is GATED on this parity staying green. Default backend stays 'python'.
findings.open_questions: retire pure-Python / flip HtlRewardSpec default — deferred until RL runs finish + explicit user OK.

findings.claim: Python's anytime/PAST-window `robustness` and the Rust forward settled-edge `StlMonitor` are DIFFERENT monitoring semantics (backward window vs bounded-future settling); they do NOT agree for streaming. Matching Python's streaming monitor requires a faithful port of the past-window semantics (eval_at::robustness_history), not the forward monitor.
findings.confidence: measured (streaming parity to 1e-9 after the port)
findings.scope: streaming HTL monitors (episode verdicts, training-metric monitors)
findings.limitations: the two modes coexist deliberately; a formula picks the mode by which monitor/evaluator it uses.
findings.framework_consequence: The Python-facing PyHtlMonitor uses robustness_history (past-window). The forward StlMonitor is for bounded-future framework-side monitoring. Do not swap one for the other expecting equal streaming numbers.

findings.claim: Past-time operators (Historically/Once/Since) belong to the ANYTIME evaluator; the forward bounded-future StlMonitor cannot settle them and MUST reject them at construction rather than mis-evaluate.
findings.scope: any StlMonitor construction
findings.limitations: past-time IS supported by robustness_history / PyHtlMonitor; the guard only blocks the forward monitor.
findings.framework_consequence: GUARD: StlMonitor::new returns MonitorError::PastTimeUnsupported on H/O/S; flatten arms are unreachable!() guarded by that check. Future forward-monitor callers get a loud error, not a wrong verdict.
findings.open_questions: past-time in the forward monitor (backward window sizing) — deferred v-next.

findings.claim: Multi-file .hymeko contexts (with @"..." imports + `using`) FAIL the naive single-file pipeline with UnresolvedRef; they require the canonical ModuleStore::compile (recursive import load into a shared interner + namespaced index + apply_usings + lower_program_to_ir). Import paths are relative to the importing file.
findings.confidence: measured (real triad_hri.hymeko now loads; was UnresolvedRef)
findings.scope: loading any imported .hymeko context
findings.limitations: a bare string has no base dir -> load_ir(str) stays single-file/import-free by design.
findings.framework_consequence: load_ir_file now routes through ModuleStore::compile; missing/broken imports surface as LoadError::Module (loud). Reuse this loader, do not re-run the single-file pipeline on imported files.
code_changes: hymeko_monitor_ir/src/lib.rs (load_ir_file via ModuleStore; LoadedIr enum; LoadError::Module)

findings.claim: HTL structural atoms can delegate to hymeko_query's pattern engine, gaining transitive-isa and signed-incidence pattern matching the trait builders cannot express. BUT the engine's compile/resolve require H:'static, so a borrowing Signal<IrState> cannot feed compile: dynamic-structure per-observe monitoring is precluded. For static contexts the structural facts are constant and computed once.
findings.scope: structural properties of a loaded (static) .hymeko context
findings.limitations: static-structure only (the 'static bound); node queries must filter Kind(Node); arity is post-filtered.
findings.framework_consequence: htl.query_atoms registered as the canonical structural-quantification path (reuse hymeko_query; builders.rs kept for cheap attrs). Dynamic-structure monitoring is an open lever (relax the monitor's 'static bound to a lifetime-parameterised trait object).
regression_tests: query_signal.rs tests (isa count, signed-ref pattern, arity, margin)
findings.open_questions: relax StlMonitor/resolve H:'static for Signal<IrState> (dynamic structure).

findings.claim: hymeko_query does NOT build with default-features=false: its always-compiled `transforms` module references the `interpret`-feature-gated `rewrite` module (an internal feature-coupling bug in that CORE crate). Consumers must keep default features.
raw_evidence: hymeko_query/src/transforms/mod.rs:233 (use crate::rewrite::...); hymeko_query/src/lib.rs:35-36 (#[cfg(feature=interpret)] pub mod rewrite)
findings.scope: any crate depending on hymeko_query
findings.limitations: hymeko_query is CORE lockdown:implementation; the fix (feature-gate transforms too, or move rewrite) is a core edit, NOT done here.
findings.framework_consequence: GUARD (recorded): depend on hymeko_query with DEFAULT features. hymeko_monitor_ir/Cargo.toml carries the note. parser is already a transitive dep so the footprint is unchanged. A future core fix should gate transforms behind interpret or move the rewrite ref.
regression_tests: the crate building at all (default features)
findings.open_questions: core fix in hymeko_query to allow a lean default-features=false consume (needs a CORE approval).

findings.claim: [SUPERSEDED 2026-07-15 by F-PP-009 — the rollout-anchor did NOT close the gap (x1=0.458); true cause is off-policy critic value-overestimation, abstraction is sound] The pick-place residual-SAC collapse (0.875 base → 0.458) is ISOLATED to F-SAC-5 (rollout-state covariate shift), NOT the critic/entropy confound. Applying the F-SAC-1/3/4 fix alone (--sac-rehab: init_alpha 0.1, lr 3e-4, ANNEAL entropy) left the critic BOUNDED (0.427 vs the AUTO run's 11-21) and α annealing, yet it STILL collapsed to 0.458 (identical Δ -0.417). So critic/entropy stabilization is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT; with a stable critic + no entropy pressure the off-policy SAC still drifts on its own rollout states. This is exactly why on-policy PPO held (trains on its own states) and off-policy SAC does not.
findings.source_experiment: 2026-07-15 pick-place RL pitfall audit (sac-rehab decisive test)
findings.confidence: measured (1 seed, 40k; identical final to the AUTO baseline with a bounded critic)
findings.scope: off-policy SAC over the residual pick-place env; confirms the coin-toss F-SAC-5 generalizes to pick-place
findings.limitations: 1 seed; the rollout-anchor fix (F-SAC-5) is being tested now to confirm it closes the gap. REFUTED by F-PP-009: rollout-anchor x1/x5/x20 and DAgger all failed; the collapse is critic overestimation, not covariate shift.
findings.framework_consequence: The rollout-state DAgger anchor (F-SAC-5) is the evidence-backed lever for pick-place off-policy RL, not just a hypothesis. Added PickResidualExpertTeacher + --sac-rehab/--rollout-anchor to pick_place_residual_rl. The kato15 vetted spec is the rollout-anchor config, not vanilla SAC.
findings.superseded_findings: corrects the flat 'pick-place RL is a negative' reading (F-PP-002/003) — the collapse was under-diagnosed confounds, not fundamental
findings.open_questions: Does the rollout-anchor (running) stop the 0.458 collapse / beat 0.875? Verdict pending; then the kato15 multi-seed run.

findings.claim: SUPERSEDES F-PP-008. The pick-place residual-SAC collapse (0.875 base -> 0.458) is OFF-POLICY CRITIC VALUE-OVERESTIMATION, NOT an abstraction/interface bug and NOT F-SAC-5 covariate shift. A 7-check abstraction audit PASSES: executed = clip(base + delta*tanh(mu), lo, hi); zero-residual reproduces base exactly (0.875, HARD GATE); teacher/base/actor read identical raw obs; the teacher residual is a FUNCTION of obs (near-obs residual gap 0.001 vs norm 0.197); the anchor lives in the same [-1,1] residual space the env receives; the target is excellent (reactive-teacher-residual closed-loop = 1.000, v3 expert = 0.958, both > base); residuals are well-calibrated. A high-capacity FEEDFORWARD BC of the reactive teacher reaches 0.792. SAC still collapses to 0.458 because the learned critic ranks the actor's own OOD near-saturated residual (|r|=0.707) at Q=-0.687 ABOVE the teacher/base/random residuals (all Q ~ -1.16..-1.22); the -Q actor loss then drives the policy off the imitation basin. Anchor-strength x5/x20 and 7-round DAgger (-> 0.58) do NOT rehabilitate it.
raw_evidence: check5 zero-residual=base 0.875; C reactive-teacher closed-loop 1.000; part4 FF-BC 0.792; check8 Q(actor)=-0.687 > Q(teacher)=-1.164
findings.confidence: measured (deterministic probes; SAC single-seed but reproduces the archived 0.458 across AUTO/rehab/anchor x1/x5-not-run/DAgger)
findings.scope: off-policy SAC over the residual pick-place env; the mechanism (critic overestimation of OOD residuals) is general to actor-critic-over-a-frozen-base
findings.limitations: SAC runs are single-seed (RL carve-out: rest ranking claims on multi-seed); the FF-BC 0.792 uses the reactive-teacher distribution; the 0.79->1.0 clone gap (recurrence?) is an open question, not resolved here.
findings.framework_consequence: Before attributing an RL collapse over a frozen base to 'RL fails' / the scenario, run the ABSTRACTION AUDIT GATE: (1) zero-residual reproduces base; (2) reactive-oracle closed-loop ceiling; (3) FF-BC of the oracle; (4) critic Q-ranking teacher vs actor vs random. Only a critic that ranks the teacher >= the actor's own action clears the RL implementation. The vetted pick-place path is IMITATION (reactive-teacher BC = 0.792, -> recurrent) + a BC-dominant/conservative-critic refiner (TD3+BC via bc_coef, or CQL/IQL/AWAC), NOT vanilla SAC + rollout anchor. kato15 is justified only once a local config beats 0.875.
code_changes: hymeko_rl/experiments/pick_place_residual_rl.py: --anchor-coef knob (proved anchor-strength inert; kept for the record)
superseded_findings: F-PP-008 (attributed the collapse to F-SAC-5 covariate shift; refuted: rollout-anchor x1 = 0.458, DAgger = 0.58, cause is critic overestimation)
open_questions: Does a recurrent residual actor close the 0.792->1.0 FF clone gap?
Does TD3+BC (bc_coef high) warm-started from the 0.792 BC clone hold >= 0.875 and refine past it?

findings.claim: Rollout-state DAgger (query the reactive teacher on the policy's OWN visited states, aggregate, re-clone) CLOSES the flat-action covariate collapse: BC 0.417 -> DAgger 0.75 median (0.625-0.792), 3 seeds, zero harmful, on the floorless PlanarGrasp coin-delivery (Gate 0 teacher-recovery 0.917).
findings.scope: flat-action reactive-teacher coin-delivery; the covariate mechanism (F-SAC-5) is general
findings.limitations: imitation recovers the teacher ceiling (~0.75 at beta=0), does not surpass it; the general loop is train.dagger.Dagger, not the experiment's private copy
findings.framework_consequence: On-policy imitation on visited states is the flat-action rescue. Canonical component = hymeko_rl/train/dagger.py::Dagger (imitation.rollout_state_dagger).
findings.open_questions: Does beta-mixing / more iters reach the ~0.9 demonstrator ceiling?

findings.claim: DAgger-anchored SAC does NOT refine past the DAgger flat policy: 0/3 seeds' online actor beats DAgger (online 0.17-0.46 vs DAgger 0.625-0.792); rollback always recovers the DAgger checkpoint. The rollout-anchor gradient is live and DOMINANT (norm 3.9-7.3 vs Q 1.7-2.6), yet the SAC objective still pulls the online policy off the greedy DAgger optimum.
findings.scope: SAC refinement on top of a DAgger-recovered flat policy
findings.limitations: AWAC/IQL and stronger refiners were de-authorized (out of scope by the hard stop)
findings.framework_consequence: Closes 'RL refinement of a DAgger flat policy expands the frontier'. The rollout anchor STABILIZES (prevents the ~0 collapse) but does not expand -> sac.rollout_state_dagger_anchor = RESEARCH_ONLY. Guard: no RL frontier-expansion claim on the flat coin-toss abstraction.

findings.claim: Dwelling into F-SAC-8: the DAgger-anchored-SAC failure is a WITHIN-SAC covariate shift, not mistuning. action_mean stays == teacher on DEMO states (demo_bc_loss 0.004) but DRIFTS 25x on the policy's own ROLLOUT states (rollout_teacher_bc_loss 0.10); the rollout anchor DOMINATES the update direction (cos_vs_full 0.965) yet LOSES, and val decays from the DAgger start (0.5-0.75) to ~0.375. Mechanism: SAC's exploration (sigma>0) breaks the self-consistency that makes DAgger work (label on GREEDY-visited states == eval states) — the anchor is computed on STOCHASTIC-rollout states while delivery is graded on the GREEDY trajectory. Exploration re-opens the covariate gap imitation removed.
findings.source_experiment: dwelling into F-SAC-8 (analysis of rollout_dagger_results.json, NO new run)
findings.confidence: MEASURED discriminants (demo 0.004 vs rollout 0.10 bc-loss, cos 0.965, val decay, 3 seeds); INFERRED exploration-covariate mechanism (not directly isolated)
findings.scope: RL refinement of an imitation-optimal policy on a floorless task
findings.limitations: The isolating cell — rollout-anchored SAC with sigma->0 (greedy rollouts) — is UNTESTED (hard stop). F-SAC-4 already showed sigma->0 WITHOUT the anchor collapses; sigma->0 WITH the anchor is the open discriminator.
findings.framework_consequence: Generalizes: exploration-based RL is self-defeating on an imitation-optimal floorless policy — exploration re-introduces the covariate shift imitation removed, and an anchor on the stochastic-rollout distribution cannot close a gap defined on the greedy-eval distribution. Guard: do not expect on-policy RL to refine a DAgger-optimal flat policy; the self-consistent greedy-DAgger loop (imitation.rollout_state_dagger) is the lever. Deepens/subsumes F-SAC-8's 'anchor dominant yet loses' into a covariate explanation.
findings.open_questions: Does sigma->0 + rollout anchor hold ~DAgger (Outcome C), confirming exploration (not -Q) as the culprit? Untested by the hard stop.
